what_it_does: When engineers design chips or circuits that trade a little accuracy for speed or power — a technique called approximate computing — they face a huge number of possible design choices to explore. Finding the best design among thousands of options is slow and expensive. This paper introduces a framework called PreDAC that first shrinks the search space by identifying and discarding poor choices before any deep search begins, then uses a formula tuned to each specific program to rank the remaining options by how well they balance cost against quality. The claim, based on the abstract alone, is faster convergence to better approximate designs.
